summary: A drop target wrapped around a real file input, with client-side accept and size checks.
useWhen: the user attaches one or more files to a form or a message
the constraints (types, size, count) should be stated before the upload is attempted rather than after

useInstead.when: a single file is picked and no drop target or file list is wanted
useInstead.why: this component adds a drop zone and a removable list; without either it is a heavier way to render the same control

useInstead.when: upload progress needs to be shown
useInstead.why: FileUpload selects files; it does not transfer them, and deliberately owns no network state

sm.use: inside a dense form, or beside other fields

md.use: the default — a standalone attachment area

guarantees: the control is a real <input type="file">, focusable and in the tab order — the drop zone is an enhancement layered on top, never the only way in
the zone is a <label> for that input, so clicking anywhere opens the picker without any script
the input is clipped to 1px rather than display:none, which would remove it from the tab order and the accessibility tree
the focus ring is drawn on the zone, where the user is looking, not on the clipped input
a polite live region announces the number of files held, because a drop changes nothing near the user's focus
dragging is signalled by a solid border as well as a colour, so it is not conveyed by colour alone (WCAG 1.4.1)
each remove button is a 24px target with a name that includes the file (WCAG 2.5.8)
requires: `label`, or an `aria-label` — an unnamed file input announces only as "button"
`hint` describing the accepted types and size limit, since `accept` itself is never announced

antiPatterns.why: both are client-side and advisory. A browser does not enforce `accept` on drop, and every platform picker offers an "All files" escape. The server must check again

antiPatterns.dont: rebuilding this as a div with onClick={() => inputRef.current.click()}
antiPatterns.why: that version has no accessible name, no tab stop, no form participation and no keyboard path — it is the usual build of this component and the usual defect

antiPatterns.dont: putting the file list inside the drop zone
antiPatterns.why: the zone is a label, so every row in it — including each remove button — would also open the file picker
it fires with the complete list after every add and every remove, never with what changed

prompt.expects: the call to action inside the zone

hint.expects: the constraints in words — "PNG or JPG, up to 5 MB"
